Operators

Stage 2 Concept ⏱ 18 min 📖 Glossary

Operators are verbs: math (+ - * / %), compare (== != < >), and combine (&& || !). Precedence decides who goes first.

🔎 Motivating questionWhy does “2 + 3 × 4” confuse even adults?

Objectives

  • Use arithmetic + comparison
  • Predict precedence
  • Use % and += correctly

Needs first: Type Conversion and Casting

1 Start with an analogy

Real life first, code second.

Canteen line with VIPs. × ÷ % go first (VIP), + − next, comparisons after, && then || last. Brackets are the teacher letting anyone jump the queue.

⚠️ Where the analogy breaksWhere it breaks: VIP order is convention, not physics. When unsure, add brackets — explicit beats clever.

2 The concept, plainly

One idea at a time, words before jargon.

Arithmetic: + - * / % (remainder). += -= *= /= %= update in place. ++ -- step by one.

Compare: == != < <= > >= give boolean. Logic: && (both), || (either), ! (flip).

&& and || short-circuit: stop early when decided — also guards null/zero safely.

3 Watch it move: VIP queue

Step at your pace. Text explains every move.

4 Live code demo

Small, correct Java 17 (LTS) code. Read, trace, copy.

Main.javaJava 17
int age = 20;
boolean teen = age >= 13 && age <= 19;
System.out.println(teen); // false
int r = 7 % 3;            // 1
int x = 5; x += 2;         // 7
System.out.println(r + " " + x);
▶ Output false 1 7
  • && needs both true; 20 fails teen.
  • 7 % 3 = 1 (leftover).
  • x += 2 means x = x + 2.
💡 Why this output?20 is not ≤19, so teen false. Remainder 1. x grows to 7.

Change values, watch consequences. Simulation — honest, not a real compiler.

6 Common mistakes (at least 3)

Wrong, why, fixed — learn from realistic slips.

❌ Mistake 1: if (x = 5) — single =.Why: = stores 5, not a question.
✅ Fix: if (x == 5).
❌ Mistake 2: 2 + 3 * 4 expected 20.Why: * first: 2+12=14.
✅ Fix: (2 + 3) * 4 for 20.
❌ Mistake 3: Comparing strings with ==.Why: == checks same house, not same text.
✅ Fix: Use word.equals(other) — next lessons.

7 Guided practice

Hints first, solutions only after a real try.

Even or odd?

Write boolean isEven for n using %.

Hintn % 2 == 0.
Solutionboolean isEven = (n % 2 == 0);
Add brackets

Rewrite 2 + 3 * 4 - 6 / 2 with brackets showing order.

Hint* / first.
Solution2 + (3*4) - (6/2) = 11.

8 Lesson quiz

3+ questions. Attempts saved locally; review queue learns your weak spots.

9 Takeaways + next step

  • % gives remainder — perfect for cycles.
  • = stores, == compares.
  • Brackets beat memorizing precedence.
🧠 Recall challengeWhat does short-circuit mean for &&?
